articleTitle: Development of CISPR 22 and second edition
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Development of EMC Standards for Information Technology Equipment
abstract: The European Norm, EN55022 is based upon CISPR Publication 22. The standard is based upon a technical rationale considering receiver density and immunity, propagation constants, ITE emission characteristics and ITE testing protocols. CISPR SC/G is now developing amendments for changes in scope, applicability, equipment classification, criteria for test sites and the development of more precise test methods to improve reproduceability, characterisation of test sites and conducted emission requirements for signal ports of ITE which connect to public and local area networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurement of emissions from distributed systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Development of EMC Standards for Information Technology Equipment
abstract: Describes the methods for the measurements of emissions from distributed systems, the results of these measurements for LANs and their effectiveness in providing a consistent repeatable method for the evaluation of the emissions from distributed systems. Immunity measurement methods are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The impact of IEC 555 on IT equipment-Part 2: Harmonics
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Development of EMC Standards for Information Technology Equipment
abstract: IEC 555 comprises a series of documents dealing with disturbances caused by equipment connected to the public low voltage supply network. There are three published documents: part 1: Definitions (IEC Publication 555-1, Guide); Part 2: Harmonics (IEC Publication 555-2, Standard); and Part 3: Voltage fluctuations and flicker (IEC Publication 555-3, Standard). Within IEC, Sub-committee 77A is responsible for the work on these documents. The changes proposed to IEC Publication 555-2, Harmonics, are likely to impact to design of almost all IT equipment up to 16 amps per phase. The author reviews the background to IEC 555-2 and considers how it may affect information technology equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some of the problems of implementing EMC standards for ITE
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Development of EMC Standards for Information Technology Equipment
abstract: Problems in implementing EMC standards for information technology equipment include different interpretations, manufacturers' understanding of the requirements, configuration problems, and variations in results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Background to the role of CISPR G in developing standards for ITE
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Development of EMC Standards for Information Technology Equipment
abstract: The International Special Committee on Radio Interference set up a new sub-committee (CISPR G) to deal with interference from information technology equipment at the Plenary meeting held in Australia in September 1985. The author outlines the work done on this subject before the formal establishment of this sub-committee. The following topics are covered: CISPR structure; working groups; Working Group 2 of CISPR Sub-Committee B; CISPR Publication 22; and immunity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of an EMC immunity standard for ITE
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Development of EMC Standards for Information Technology Equipment
abstract: The author outlines the history and politics of the development of an EMC immunity standard for ITE and describes the technical work of CISPR Sub-Committee G. A draft version of Part 1 of Publication 24, which defines a set of phenomena for establishing an intrinsic level of immunity on ITE products to enable them to operate normally in their intended environments, is appended to the paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Development of EMC Standards for Information Technology Equipment
abstract: Using the 'representative system' concept, a new test strategy has been developed, whereby the EMC performance of large systems may be determined under controlled conditions, prior to installation at customer premises. The effects of future extensions and upgrades may be examined for their impact on the EMC performance of the system without the need for costly retesting at the system level.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
